passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: The enacted text of the bill he voted for and co-sponsored; the added section 15-2401.01 makes every student eligible to enroll in an Arizona public school a qualified student.
Bill overview listing him as a co-sponsor of the same instrument, signed as Chapter 388.

rows.reasoning: Kavanagh co-sponsored and voted Aye on HB 2853 (2022), a single-subject empowerment scholarship account bill whose added section 15-2401.01 makes "qualified student" include every resident "eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" in kindergarten or "Any of grades one through twelve", with the department transferring the student's state funding into the account for tuition at a qualified (nongovernmental) school. That enacts "universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family" rather than a program "open to a wider range of families under an income cap". Under the V5 earlier-chamber ruling his 2022 House record counts for the Senate seat.
